  - paragraph: "Objective: Detect when graphs mislead by checking scales, intervals and 3D effects, and explain the change accurately."

  - 'heading "1 OBSERVE: Compare the graphs" [level=2]'
  - paragraph: Study the honest and manipulated graphs of the same data.
  - table:
    - rowgroup:
      - 'row "Data: Ice cream sales (cups) Jan Feb Mar Apr May"':
        - 'columnheader "Data: Ice cream sales (cups)"'
        - columnheader "Jan"
        - columnheader "Feb"
        - columnheader "Mar"
        - columnheader "Apr"
        - columnheader "May"
      - row "100 150 200 250 300":
        - cell
        - cell "100"
        - cell "150"
        - cell "200"
        - cell "250"
        - cell "300"
  - article:
    - heading "HONEST GRAPH (not misleading)" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Y-axis starts at 0 with equal intervals.
    - img "Ice cream sales graph": 0 70 140 210 280 350 100 Jan 150 Feb 200 Mar 250 Apr 300 May
  - article:
    - heading "MANIPULATED GRAPH (misleading)" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Notice how the change looks much bigger.
    - img "Ice cream sales graph": 100 140 180 220 260 300 100 Jan 150 Feb 200 Mar 250 Apr 300 May
  - article:
    - 'heading "2 MANIPULATE: Create misleading graphs" [level=2]'
    - paragraph: Toggle options to see how graphs can mislead.
    - text: 1 Truncated Y-axis Start the Y-axis above 0.
    - checkbox "Truncated Y-axis" [checked]
    - combobox "Start at":
      - option "0"
      - option "50"
      - option "100" [selected]
      - option "150"
    - combobox "Maximum":
      - option "300" [selected]
      - option "350"
      - option "400"
    - text: 2 Unequal Intervals Use unequal gaps between values.
    - checkbox "Unequal intervals"
    - combobox "Compress lower end":
      - option "None" [selected]
      - option "Strong"
    - combobox "Stretch upper end":
      - option "None" [selected]
      - option "Strong"
    - text: 3 3D Distortion Use 3D style to exaggerate change.
    - checkbox "3D distortion"
    - combobox "Chart style":
      - option "2D (Flat)" [selected]
      - option "3D Perspective"
    - text: "Current settings: Truncated Y-axis (100 to 300)"
  - article:
    - heading "LIVE MANIPULATED GRAPH" [level=2]
    - img "Ice cream sales graph": 100 140 180 220 260 300 100 Jan 150 Feb 200 Mar 250 Apr 300 May
    - complementary: This graph exaggerates the change. The Y-axis doesn't start at 0.
  - 'heading "3 NOTICE THE PATTERN: What makes a graph misleading?" [level=2]'
  - article:
    - text: Truncated Axis
    - paragraph: Starting the axis above 0 makes the same change look bigger.
    - strong: "Example: Start at 100 instead of 0."
  - article:
    - text: Unequal Intervals
    - paragraph: Unequal gaps between values distort the real pattern of change.
    - strong: "Example: Bigger gaps at the top."
  - article:
    - text: 3D Distortion
    - paragraph: 3D effects add depth that exaggerates the visual change.
    - strong: "Example: 3D bars or perspective."
  - article:
    - heading "4 UNDERSTAND THE RULE" [level=2]
    - heading "Key Rule" [level=3]
    - paragraph: A graph is misleading if the scales, intervals, or 3D effects exaggerate or hide the real change.
    - paragraph: ✓ Does the axis start at 0? ✓ Are the intervals equal? ✓ Is the graph 2D (flat)?
    - complementary:
      - text: COMMON MISCONCEPTION
      - paragraph: A steep line or tall bar always means a big change.
  - article:
    - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
    - table:
      - rowgroup:
        - row "Month Jan Feb Mar Apr May":
          - columnheader "Month"
          - columnheader "Jan"
          - columnheader "Feb"
          - columnheader "Mar"
          - columnheader "Apr"
          - columnheader "May"
        - row "Sales (cups) 100 150 200 250 300":
          - rowheader "Sales (cups)"
          - cell "100"
          - cell "150"
          - cell "200"
          - cell "250"
          - cell "300"
    - complementary:
      - text: Honest Graph
      - paragraph: "Y-axis: 0 to 350 Equal intervals of 50 Real increase = 200 cups"
      - strong: "Conclusion: Real increase is 200 cups."
    - complementary:
      - text: Manipulated Graph (Truncated Axis)
      - paragraph: "Y-axis: 100 to 300 Looks like a very steep increase Data is the same"
      - strong: "Verdict: Misleading. Axis is truncated."
    - text: "Evidence-based verdict: The manipulated graph exaggerates the change by truncating the Y-axis."
  - 'heading "5 TRY INDEPENDENTLY: Your turn" [level=2]'
  - paragraph: Decide if the graph is misleading. Choose the reason and explain using evidence.
  - img "Independent misleading graph": 160 168 176 184 192 200 170 Week 1 175 Week 2 180 Week 3 185 Week 4

    - text: Yes, it is misleading

    - text: No, it is not misleading
  - group "Select the reason":

    - radio "Truncated axis" [checked]
    - text: Truncated axis
    - radio "Unequal intervals"
    - text: Unequal intervals
    - radio "3D distortion"
    - text: 3D distortion
    - radio "Other"
    - text: Other
  - text: Explain using evidence
  - textbox "Evidence explanation": The Y-axis starts at 160 instead of 0. This makes the increase from 170 to 185 look bigger than it really is.
  - button "Check verdict"
  - complementary:
    - text: Your verdict
    - paragraph:
      - img
      - text: Correct
